questions.cardText:
[Musicology] What is a tritone interval often referred to as in music?
A. Perfect fifth
B. Minor third
C. Devil’s interval
Answer: C. Due to its dissonant sound, the tritone interval is famously used in the opening theme of “The Simpsons” (between the first two melody notes: “The Simp-”) to introduce the audience to its unsettling and chaotic world.
questions.de: Welchen Beinamen, lateinisch „diabolus in musica“, trägt das dissonante Intervall des Tritonus oft?
questions.en: What nickname, 'diabolus in musica' in Latin, does the dissonant tritone interval often carry?
questions.answerEn: The devil's interval (the devil in music)

timeline.labelEn: Andreas Werckmeister cites 'diabolus in musica' as a name used by the old authorities for the tritone
timeline.labelDe: Andreas Werckmeister zitiert „diabolus in musica“ als Bezeichnung der alten Autoritäten für den Tritonus

questions.notes: Wikipedia lists 'the Devil's interval' as an (obscure) other name; 'diabolus in musica' used since at least the early 18th century. Simpsons claim not confirmed on a fetched page (the theme is in the Lydian dominant scale per Wikipedia); the tritone there lies between the 1st and 3rd notes (C–F♯ on 'The Simp-sons'), not the first two (C–E) as the card says.

questions.cardText:
[Literature] “Stream of consciousness” is a literary technique used to:
A. Depict characters’ thoughts and feelings without interruption
B. Tell a story chronologically
C. Describe a way the author narrates a storyline in a free-flow format
Answer: A.
questions.de: Wie heißt die literarische Technik, die den Fluss der Gedanken und Gefühle einer Figur ohne Unterbrechung wiedergibt, ein Begriff aus der Psychologie von William James?
questions.en: What is the literary technique called that depicts a character's flow of thoughts and feelings without interruption, a term borrowed from William James's psychology?

timeline.labelEn: May Sinclair first applies 'stream of consciousness' to literature in The Egoist
timeline.labelDe: May Sinclair verwendet „Bewusstseinsstrom“ in The Egoist erstmals für die Literatur

questions.notes: Term coined in psychology by William James (1890); first applied to literature by May Sinclair (The Egoist, April 1918) about Dorothy Richardson's Pilgrimage.
